title: Merge Strategies & Conflict Resolution
learning_objectives: Understand three merge strategies: merge commit, squash, rebase
Identify when merge conflicts occur and why they happen
Resolve merge conflicts using VS Code or command-line tools
Choose appropriate merge strategy for different CatchBook scenarios
Execute merge via GitHub web interface and command line
Understand fast-forward merges vs three-way merges
Clean up merged branches locally and remotely
Complete first feature branch merge to CatchBook main
outline: Introduction: Merging strategies and their tradeoffs
What is merging? Integrating divergent branch histories
Merge strategy 1: Merge commit (preserves full history)
Merge strategy 2: Squash and merge (clean linear history)
Merge strategy 3: Rebase and merge (linear history, preserves commits)
When to use each strategy: CatchBook examples
Fast-forward merges: when branches haven't diverged
Three-way merges: when branches have diverged
What are merge conflicts? Same file, same lines, different changes
Resolving conflicts in VS Code: choose incoming, current, or both
Resolving conflicts on command line: manual editing + git add
Hands-on: Create intentional conflict in CatchBook README
Resolving the conflict and completing merge
Testing after merge: always verify functionality
Cleaning up: `git branch -d feature/branch-name`, `git push -d origin feature/branch-name`
Post-merge workflow: pull main, verify, delete local branch
Hands-on: Complete CatchBook PR merge workflow end-to-end

catchbook_context.feature: Safe merge workflows for CatchBook feature integration
catchbook_context.deliverable: Merge feature/update-readme PR to main, resolve conflicts if any, clean up branches

criteria: Successfully merge feature branch into main via GitHub PR
Intentionally create and resolve a merge conflict
Explain when to use squash vs merge commit for CatchBook
Clean up local and remote feature branches post-merge
Verify main branch contains merged changes
Articulate merge strategy tradeoffs (history preservation vs clean log)

professor_constraints: Show conflict markers visually before explaining
Demonstrate VS Code merge conflict UI (most beginner-friendly)
Create realistic CatchBook conflict scenario (two people editing README)
Emphasize testing after merge (never merge blindly)
Explain squash is preferred for CatchBook feature branches (clean history)
Show git log --graph before and after merge to visualize
Address common fear: conflicts are normal, not disasters
Preview rebase but defer deep coverage to advanced Git topics (Phase 25)
